Viggle is doing something seriously impressive, and I think creators should pay attention! 🔥

What makes Viggle Remake stand out isn't just its ability to transform videos. It's how much creative control it gives you over an existing scene.

Unlike many AI video tools that focus primarily on generating clips from scratch, Viggle lets you take an existing video and fundamentally reinvent it.

Here's what makes it different:

🎬 Full Character Recasting: Replace every character in a scene while maintaining character consistency across multiple cuts.

🎭 Beyond Face Swapping: Change entire characters, not just their faces. Reimagine who appears in your videos.

🌍 Scene Transformation: Swap objects, change backgrounds, restyle environments, and introduce new visual effects.

⏱️ Up to 2-Minute Videos: Work with longer sequences rather than being restricted to short clips.

💬 Conversational Editing: Keep chatting with the AI to correct individual shots, refine results, and get the scene exactly how you want it.

🔓 Open Weights: Viggle is releasing its model weights, giving the AI community more opportunities to explore and build with the technology.

💰 Affordable Creation: Starting at $0.96 per 10 seconds at 720p.

But here's what I find particularly exciting: Viggle is shifting the focus from generating a video to having the power to remake an entire video.

That's a major creative advantage for filmmakers, advertisers, storytellers, and AI content creators.

Big respect to the Viggle team for pushing the boundaries and opening up this technology to the community.

There’s a lot to say, and as always, I’ll try to keep it nuanced and kind.

First things first: I love Nut and Hong dearly. I’ve been here for two years, and I’ve supported them every step of the way, in everything they’ve done together and apart. I love them as people and as artists, first and foremost. I believe they’re good people, and they have only ever shown kindness and warmth to the queer community. I believe in equity and fairness, and I will never ask anyone to disclose their identity or prove their queerness. I also don’t believe you need to be queer to portray queer characters.

That being said, if you choose to portray queer characters, I need you to commit to them. If you take on queer roles, especially characters who are canonically in love, you can’t erase that part of their story. Way and Night may not be together in 21, but the romantic subtext is clearly there: Way’s jealousy of Ai, the heavy flirting, Night already being in love with Way. I’m not saying any of this will be erased in 21. The show isn’t out and hasn’t even started filming, so we have no idea what it will become. And that’s part of the problem. It’s the same problem we’ve been living with for the past year.

The uncertainty, the “will they, won’t they,” is what has brought us here: tearing each other apart over bromance debates, with accusations flying in both directions.

One thing I enjoy about exploring Web3 is seeing how different projects solve different problems instead of following the same direction.

@rarelistio makes creator participation more meaningful by connecting quality contributions with campaign opportunities and recognition.

@fomopoly_rh brings another dimension to gaming by combining virtual property ownership, trading and an evolving in-game economy.

Meanwhile, @agentdojo explores the possibilities of AI-powered gaming, where training, memory and strategy influence how fighters develop.

What connects these ecosystems is their willingness to experiment with new ways of involving users.

Whether it's creating, owning or training, each offers a different experience worth understanding.

I'm keeping an eye on how these projects grow and what they bring to the Web3 space.

Morning Lovelies 🤎

Web3 gaming is exploring more than one way to make players part of the experience.

@fomopoly_rh connects virtual land ownership with an economic system involving property trading, stock generation, and $DEAL. The interesting part is how these elements work together to give the city its own in-game economy.

@agentdojo takes a different approach by bringing trainable AI fighters into turn-based competition. Players can shape agents with individual personalities, memories, and combat styles before testing them in the arena.

One centres on the relationship between digital property and economic activity, while the other explores AI customisation and competitive gameplay.

Both offer interesting concepts to follow as Web3 gaming continues to develop.

Exploring and sharing my discoveries through @rarelistio .

Open models are only half open if one company runs the servers.
That company can change them, price them or switch them off.

@LightchainAI is a blockchain built for AI. Independent operators serve open models like gpt-oss, Qwen3 and Llama from their own GPUs, and the chain picks who serves each job. Every job leaves a public record (job ID, transaction, worker) on https://t.co/4CfdskTksr.
Your prompt is encrypted before it touches the chain.

I tried it myself. I asked: What makes LightChain AI different from ChatGPT? Not a ChatGPT replacement. A different setup, where the servers are independent and every job leaves a record you can look up.

Try it: https://t.co/Ud79GYwZEr

Voice AI is now good enough that preference and human-likeness can be scored as separate targets.

@voicearena_ai launched a new benchmark, Turing TTS to score the second one directly: listeners hear the same sentence from a person and from a model, then pick the person.

How often they pick the model is the Fool Rate. 50% would mean listeners can’t tell.

Even the best model, Gemini 3.8 Flash TTS, fooled them about 10% of the time.

On Voice Arena’s preference board, the top four models are statistically tied. Measured against a human, the whole field still has a long way to go.
